context.problem: Choose the primary application database for Gleanmo, independently of framework and application language.
constraints: Compare primary application databases. A separate analytics engine can be evaluated later.
Holding the application language and framework constant isolates the database decision.
The existing PostgreSQL storage backing for XTDB is distinct from using PostgreSQL directly.
Define required history preservation before evaluating migration risk.

completion_guidance.blank_values: Null weights and scores are unassessed, not zero. Empty notes and conclusions await user input.
completion_guidance.weights: Set each weight to low, medium, or high when ready.
completion_guidance.scores: Use 0 through 5, with higher scores always indicating a better fit. For effort, cost, risk, and churn, lower burden scores higher.
completion_guidance.comparison: Assess migration costs separately from ongoing benefits. Record concrete stack and hosting assumptions in option notes before scoring.
completion_guidance.ownership: The user will provide assessments. No option has been ranked or selected.

options.label: XTDB 1.x
options.description: Retain the current XTDB 1.x database and data model. This option does not imply upgrading to XTDB 2.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Use PostgreSQL directly as the application database, with an explicit relational schema.

options.label: SQLite
options.description: Use SQLite directly as the application database, with an explicit relational schema.

options.label: Datomic
options.description: Use Datomic as the application database. Specify the deployment edition and topology before assessment.

criteria.label: Query clarity
criteria.description: Ease of expressing and understanding application queries.

criteria.label: Analytics access
criteria.description: Ease of expressing aggregates, time series, and exploratory analysis. External tool connectivity belongs under interoperability.

criteria.label: Data inspection
criteria.description: Ease of inspecting records and diagnosing unexpected data.

criteria.label: Performance predictability
criteria.description: Ease of anticipating, measuring, and controlling query costs as data grows.

criteria.label: Data integrity
criteria.description: Support for transactions, constraints, relationships, and concurrent updates.

criteria.label: Schema evolution
criteria.description: Ease of changing the data model while preserving existing records.

criteria.label: Temporal/history needs
criteria.description: Fit for the history, audit, and temporal queries Gleanmo actually needs.

criteria.label: Operational simplicity
criteria.description: Burden of hosting, backups, restores, upgrades, and routine administration.

criteria.label: Migration effort
criteria.description: Work needed to port data, queries, mutations, integrations, and tests.

criteria.label: Migration risk
criteria.description: Risk of data loss, semantic changes, downtime, and incomplete rollback during migration.

criteria.label: Ecosystem longevity
criteria.description: Expected durability of maintenance, expertise, libraries, and support.

criteria.label: Interoperability and portability
criteria.description: Ease of moving hosts, connecting analytics tools, or replacing the application while retaining the database. Consider language drivers, protocols, connectors, and framework coupling.
